names.official: Republic of the Union of Myanmar

summary: Myanmar's eVisa portal says nationals of the countries on its list can apply for a tourist eVisa allowing a stay of 28 days, valid only for entry at the Yangon, Mandalay and Nay Pyi Taw international airports and the Kawthaung land border checkpoint. It says ordinary passport holders of Brunei, Cambodia, Indonesia, Laos, the Philippines, Thailand and Vietnam need no visa for tourist visits up to their exemption period through those airports, and Singaporeans for up to 30 days through all international checkpoints; Myanmar's Foreign Ministry also lists ordinary-passport exemptions for Belarus, Russia and Malaysia. Canada says land crossings may close with little or no notice or be restricted to nationals of neighbouring states, and the UK advises against all travel to parts of the country.

notes: The UK government says there are strict regulations around bringing in and using drones and that you should not attempt to enter Myanmar with a drone unless you have the necessary permits in place before you travel. Australia's Smartraveller says drones have been seized by customs officials and tourists have been arrested for operating them.

The UK government says that on arrival you must declare any valuable articles, including gold, gems and jewellery, to customs, and that you cannot import gold or gold bullion into Myanmar for trading. Canada says it is illegal to export gems and that a permit is required to purchase or possess cultural or archaeological artifacts.

payments.text: The UK government says Myanmar is largely a cash-based society, that many ATMs do not accept international bank cards and many commercial outlets will only accept cash, and to phone ahead if you want to pay a hotel or restaurant by card. Canada says U.S. currency is widely accepted but only as new, unmarked and undamaged notes, and that it is illegal to exchange currency at unauthorized locations.

safety.text: Canada says the conflict between military forces and armed groups has escalated since October 2023, with indiscriminate regime airstrikes causing civilian casualties and reports of increased drone strikes, and advises avoiding all travel to Myanmar; the UK advises against all travel to parts of the country. The UK says some areas are under martial law and others have curfews or stay-at-home orders, and both governments warn of a risk of arbitrary detention.

tips.text: Canada advises avoiding all travel to Myanmar and Australia says do not travel; the UK advises against all travel to parts of the country, including Chin, Kachin and Rakhine states and Shan State North, and against all but essential travel to Mandalay Region. Canada reports indiscriminate regime airstrikes and drone strikes, and says its officials require permission from the Myanmar government to travel freely outside Yangon.

Canada strongly advises against all travel to Myanmar, including through its land borders, and says border crossings may close with little or no notice and entry may be restricted to nationals of the bordering states. Myanmar's eVisa portal says eVisa holders may enter only via the Yangon, Mandalay and Nay Pyi Taw international airports and the Kawthaung land border checkpoint.

The UK government says Myanmar is largely a cash-based society and many ATMs do not accept international bank cards, that US dollars should be in good condition with no pen marks, folds or tears, and that exchange counters may refuse dollars with the letters AB and CB at the start of the serial number.

The UK government says the Myanmar authorities control internet access and periodically cut off access entirely, and that some services, including Facebook and WhatsApp, are blocked and inaccessible without VPNs.
The UK government says you should remove shoes and socks before entering a pagoda or monastery, and that shorts, short skirts and sleeveless tops can cause offence when visiting religious sites.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Myanmar?
faq.answer: Yes, unless you hold an ordinary passport of Brunei, Cambodia, Indonesia, Laos, the Philippines or Thailand (tourist visits of up to 14 days, entering and departing through the Yangon, Mandalay or Naypyidaw international airports), of Vietnam (30 days, through the same airports) or of Singapore (30 days, through all international checkpoints), according to the eVisa portal. Myanmar's Foreign Ministry also lists ordinary-passport exemptions for Belarus and Russia (30 days) and Malaysia (14 days). Nationals of the countries on the eVisa portal's list, including the US, the UK and Australia, can apply for the 28-day tourist eVisa. For other nationalities, Myanmar's Embassy in Kuwait says a foreign national is required to apply and obtain a visa in advance at Myanmar's missions abroad before entering the country; the Foreign Ministry lists the tourist visa at 40 USD for a stay of 28 days.

faq.question: Can I enter Myanmar overland?
faq.answer: Canada strongly advises against all travel to Myanmar, including through its land borders, and says border crossings may close with little or no notice and entry may be restricted to nationals of the bordering states. Myanmar's eVisa portal says eVisa holders may enter only via the Yangon, Mandalay and Nay Pyi Taw international airports and the Kawthaung international land border checkpoint.

faq.question: Is Myanmar safe to visit?
faq.answer: Canada advises avoiding all travel to Myanmar and Australia says do not travel; the UK advises against all travel to parts of the country. Canada says that since October 2023 the conflict has escalated, with indiscriminate regime airstrikes causing civilian casualties and reports of increased drone strikes, and that improvised explosive devices and drones have been used in Yangon, Mandalay and Nay Pyi Taw.

faq.question: How long does the Myanmar eVisa take?
faq.answer: Myanmar's eVisa portal says processing takes a minimum of 3 working days (Myanmar time) for a normal tourist visa, starting when the application acknowledgement email is sent after you submit and pay online. Its FAQ says you are currently required to print out the eVisa approval letter and present it to the immigration officer on arrival.

faq.question: Can I extend a Myanmar tourist visa?
faq.answer: No. Myanmar's eVisa FAQ says the tourist eVisa cannot be extended; if your most recent visa is a business eVisa, you can apply for an extension through the eStay system. No official source we could read states the overstay penalty.
